claims.explanation: TW-37 is a BH3-mimetic that inhibits the anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family proteins BCL-2, BCL-XL, and MCL1, so selectivity likely reflects which anti-apoptotic proteins the tumor depends on for survival. Lines with loss of PTEN/PIK3CA activation, KRAS/BRAF-driven MAPK signaling, or high MCL1/BCL2/BCL2L1 expression are expected to be more dependent on these proteins and thus more sensitive, whereas intact apoptotic effectors and low dependence on BCL-2 family proteins confer resistance.

features.basis: PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling and increases dependence on anti-apoptotic BCL-2 proteins; PTEN-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines
PIK3CA activation drives survival signaling and dependence on BCL-2 family anti-apoptotic proteins
KRAS-driven MAPK signaling upregulates MCL1 and other anti-apoptotic proteins, creating dependence on BCL-2 family inhibition
BRAF-driven MAPK signaling increases MCL1 dependence, sensitizing to BH3 mimetics
TW-37 binds MCL1 with high affinity; tumors with high MCL1 expression depend on it for survival
TW-37 was designed to target BCL-2; high BCL2 expression predicts dependence and sensitivity
TW-37 binds BCL-XL; high BCL2L1 expression may indicate dependence on this anti-apoptotic protein
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not a strong predictor; intact p53 may enhance apoptosis in some contexts
SMAD4 mutation appears enriched in resistant lines, possibly reflecting a less apoptotic-prone state
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines and may reflect alternative survival dependencies
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines, possibly linking chromatin remodeling to apoptotic priming
KMT2C mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, suggesting a role in apoptotic priming
